title: Day 90
hook: Ninety days. You did this, one small day at a time.

screens.text: **Ninety days, {{convert.first_name}}.** Ninety days ago you opened Day 1, maybe nervous, maybe alone, not sure what came next. Look where you are now.
None of it had to be perfect. You did it anyway.

events.title: You said yes
events.text: Your shahada, and a slate wiped clean.

events.title: Wudu and your first prayer
events.text: You learned wudu and prayed from your first day.

events.title: A masjid, a mentor, people
events.text: You walked into the masjid, prayed in a row, and started building your circle.

events.title: The whole prayer
events.text: Every phrase of the prayer, al-Fatiha and a short surah.

events.title: Your story, out loud
events.text: You told your story and explained the basics to someone who asked.

events.title: Slumps and hard questions
events.text: You made it through the low patches and the hard questions, and you kept coming back.

screens.title: Your Day-90 check: tick what's true for you today
steps: Pray with confidence: I pray the five prayers on my own, with every phrase
Pray with confidence: I can pray behind an imam and join late
Talk about Islam: I can tell my story and the basics in two minutes
Talk about Islam: I'm okay saying "I don't know, let me find out"
Not overwhelmed: I know what's required and what can wait
Not overwhelmed: I know a low patch isn't leaving Islam
Belong: I have a mentor or imam I can reach
Belong: I have at least one Muslim friend, and a place to be for Eid
screens.done_text: What you ticked is real. What you didn't is your next step, not a failure. The guide can help with any of them.

screens.text: **Say alhamdulillah.** Allah says that if you're grateful, He will give you more [Q 14:7]. Gratitude (*shukr*) for these 90 days isn't bragging. It's noticing that Allah carried you through each one.
bubbles: And remember the first lesson: your slate was wiped clean on the day you said yes [Muslim 121]. Everything since has been building on that.

screens.text: Tap once for each thing from these 90 days you're grateful for, and say it as you tap.

screens.prompt: Read your Day 1 answer: what made you say yes? Then your Day 30 and Day 60 reflections. What's changed? What are you most proud of?

screens.title: Islam was never a 90-day course. This was just the start. Tap to see what doesn't end today.

cards.back: The AI guide, and every lesson, to re-read any time.
The plan you made yesterday, with reminders.
Ramadan, Eid and the other seasons: the app will still walk you through them when they come.

screens.prompt: Write a letter to yourself, to open in six months. What do you want future-you to remember about these 90 days? What do you hope you're still doing? What would you say to them on a hard day? The app will show it to you again.

screens.optional_extra: Do something small to celebrate: a favorite meal, a walk, or time with your people. You earned it.

screens.text: You pray, you can talk about your faith, you know what matters now, and you have people. Keep going, a little at a time.
The best deeds are the ones you keep doing, even small ones [Bukhari 6464]. Ninety days in, you're still here. Slow and steady, for life.

check.prompt: You didn't tick every item in your Day-90 check. What does that mean?

options.text: Those items are your next steps, not a failure
options.feedback: Right. Everyone keeps growing after Day 90. Pick one and work on it with your mentor.

options.text: You should restart the program from Day 1
options.feedback: Not quite. No restart needed. Re-read any lesson you want, and keep moving forward.

check.prompt: What does the Qur'an promise to those who are grateful?

options.feedback: Right [Q 14:7]. Gratitude opens the door to more good.

options.text: Nothing; gratitude is just good manners
options.feedback: Not quite. Allah promises increase to the grateful [Q 14:7].

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- The four Day-90 outcomes: prays with confidence (alone and at the masjid), talks about Islam without freezing, isn't overwhelmed, belongs to a community (Spec §2).
- Gratitude brings increase [Q 14:7]. Regular small deeds are most beloved to Allah [Bukhari 6464]. The strong believer is better, and there's good in both; seek Allah's help and don't give up [Muslim 2664].
- Islam wiped out what came before [Muslim 121]; the door of mercy stays open [Q 39:53].
- After Day 90: the guide, all lessons, calendar modules (Ramadan, Eid and the rest), the Day 89 plan and the mentor all continue.

**Likely questions**
- *"What next?"* Point to their Day 89 plan; suggest the outcome they ticked least as the focus; one small step at a time.
- *"I didn't tick everything."* Normal and fine. Help them pick one item and a concrete next step; offer to re-open the relevant lesson (O1: Days 22, 30, 86; O2: Days 23, 28, 85; O3: Days 12, 29, 89; O4: Days 18, 87).
- *"How can I help the next new Muslim?"* Day 80: volunteering, being the friend they needed, offering to sit with a new convert at the masjid. Through the masjid's own programs.
- *"I feel sad it's over."* Validate. Nothing is ending but the daily unlock; the guide, the lessons and the people stay.

**Escalate:** nothing specific.

**Don't**
- Don't grade or rank the convert, and never share their check results.
- Don't suggest public sharing or posting the milestone; they decide who knows (Spec §3).
- Don't use the milestone to push extra obligations.
sourcesMd:
- Qur'an [14:7](https://quran.com/14/7): if you are grateful, I will surely increase you.
- [Bukhari 6464](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6464): the deeds Allah loves most are the regular ones, even if small.
- [Muslim 2664](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2664): the strong believer; seek Allah's help and don't give up.
- [Muslim 121](https://sunnah.com/muslim:121): Islam wipes out what came before it.
- Qur'an [39:53](https://quran.com/39/53): don't despair of Allah's mercy.
- The New Muslims Field Guide ch. 9 (slow and steady).
